surface_mechanism_description: Ligand exchange between TMA and surface hydroxyl groups followed by water pulse to regenerate OH sites
evidence: Upon TEMAH exposure (first half-cycle), 30% of the surface hydrogen is reacted and a weak Si–O–Hf band appears at 1000 cm−1, as previously observed. However, while water-vapor pulses leave the surface unchanged at 100 °C growth temperature, the first ozone pulse removes all the remaining surface hydrogen and strongly oxidizes the Si interface. The second TEMAH pulse fully completes the Si–O–Hf interface (growth of the 1000 cm−1 band), while water-based ALD required 5–7 cycles to reach a similar (final) interface configuration. The right panel of Fig. 2 confirms that the expected ligand exchange (CHx stretching modes of methyl and ethyl groups of TEMAH at 2800–3000 cm−1) takes place during ozone-based growth. Importantly, there is no evidence for hydroxyl groups (see inset at bottom right of Fig. 2) after each ozone exposure. The fact that the surface is not OH terminated is the most likely reason for the lower growth rate, since the TEMAH precursor cannot react as readily with the surface after the ozone pulse. Instead, carboxylic and nitro compounds appear (or are removed) on the surface after each ozone (or TEMAH) exposure as evidenced by the alternating gain and loss of the multiple IR modes at 1280, 1588, 1614, 1654, and 1692 cm−1 (not shown). These oxidized carbon and nitrogen species may serve as nucleation sites for TEMA H attachment, with less reactivity compared to the hydroxyl groups.
